prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1230; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed head-on collision; the insured reports the claimant's vehicle crossed into their lane on a straight road. Claim file opened and assigned for review.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage period.

Entry 3: Photos taken at the scene show the front-end damage on both vehicles, and the damage pattern matches the described impact. No prior damage to the vehicle is noted in our records or the photos.

Entry 4: Police report obtained; it confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. No independent witnesses were identified, so the account rests on the parties and the physical evidence.

Entry 5: Claimant's counsel notified us of representation and requested that all contact go through their office. Initial recorded statement scheduled.

Entry 6: Recorded statement taken from the claimant through counsel. Account of the collision is consistent with the first notice and with what the claimant described at the scene.

Entry 7: Medical records received reporting a back strain. The reported injury is plausible for a collision of this type, and no earlier injury to the same body area is known from the records reviewed.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a usual course of care and tapered as the patient improved. Follow-up notes show steady progress with no unexpected changes in the treatment plan.

Entry 9: Claimant's account was reviewed again through counsel and remains the same as in every prior conversation, including the statement and the call with the adjuster. No inconsistencies have been identified.

Entry 10: File reviewed against photos, police report, policy records, and medical notes. All items are consistent with the reported loss; file remains open pending final medical summary from treating provider.
